+title: Send subagent_update before the first event of each child run
+---
+## What
+When an agent run starts, send one `subagent_update` on the PARENT ACP session. It must go out before any request or event that uses the child id (RFD rule: the agent must not guess parentage and must not move an issued interaction to an other session).
+
+Fields: `update.sessionId` (child id from `SubagentSessionTable`), `title` (agent name), `description` (agent description), `capabilities: { cancel: {} }`, `state`, `cwd`, `additionalDirectories`. Later sends carry only changed fields. An omitted field is unchanged and `null` clears it.
+
+Hook: `AgentsComposition.makeRunEventObserver` (`Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Tools/AgentsComposition.swift`) today only calls `runCallJoins.recordAgentRunEvent`. Add the announce there, or in a new `SubagentAnnouncer` in `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SubagentAnnouncer.swift`. The observer is synchronous and must not wait, so the announcer hands the send to an ordered async queue that keeps the order: announce first, then events.
+
+Needs: the wire type `SessionUpdate.subagentUpdate` does not exist in FoundationModelsACP yet (the generated `SessionUpdate` union has no such case). That is a change in a sibling package. Do NOT add it from this task. Wait for the card on FoundationModelsACP (to be discussed with the user first), or use a local type if the user decides so.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The first wire message that carries a child id is a `subagent_update` for that id, on the parent session id.
+- [ ] For a nested run, the update goes on the child id of the parent run, and the parent is announced first.
+- [ ] A second event of the same run sends no second full announcement; a changed `state` sends a patch.
+- [ ] No announcement is sent when the connection is closed or the session is closed.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/SubagentAnnouncerTests.swift`: order of announce before events, nested order, patch only on change, using a stub model that starts an agent run.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter SubagentAnnouncerTests`. All pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #subagents
\ No newline at end of file

+- actor: wballard
+  id: 01m6gp1x3kjxzzjcp1zkenv77c
+  text: |-
+    DECISION (user, 2026-11-03): the agent is a session AND a tool, so it has the behaviors of both. ACP does not link the tool call to the child session, so we add a link in `_meta`, using the SAH extension pattern of the wire package (FoundationModelsACP `SAH/SAHMeta.swift`: payload types under `_meta.sah`). Card for the payload type: see the FoundationModelsACP board, "SAH meta payload that links an agent tool call and its child session".
+    THE LINK:
+    - On the `subagent_update` of a child: `_meta.sah.agentRun = { toolCallId }`, the id of the `agents` tool call that started the child (the SDK tool call id; the Router record has it as `agentSpawn.parentToolCallId`).
+    - On the `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` of that `agents` call: `_meta.sah.agentRun = { sessionId }`, the child session id.
+    THE REMOVAL RULE: a finished child is removed. ACP has no removal message. The agent sends none. The CLIENT removes a child from the tree when its linked tool call reaches a final status (completed, failed or cancelled). The agent must therefore send the final `tool_call_update` AFTER the last update of the child and after its final `state_update` (idle), so the client never drops a child that still has traffic coming.
+    AGENT: put the link on both messages; keep the order above; the link is also sent in the replay and in the post-response snapshots of a restored child. A child that has no known tool call (a host-started run) carries no link, and stays until its parent closes.
+    CLIENT: read the link; `SessionModel` gets `startedByToolCallId` and a tool call entry gets `childSession`; remove the child (set `isClosed`) when the linked tool call is final; keep the child if the link is missing.
+    VIEWS: the `agents` tool row in the parent thread is a link that jumps to the child session while it exists; after removal the row stays as history and shows the result.
+    Acceptance criteria to add: the link is on both messages; the child is removed on the final tool call status; no child traffic after its removal; a child without a link is not removed; replay and snapshots carry the link; cancel through `tool_call/cancel` and through `session/cancel` on the child id reach the same run.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m6h3jxwcx6cjtpjhxrbx4rbt
+  text: |-
+    DISCOVERIES (before the code).
+    1. The observer gets (AgentRun, SessionOutput) from the events of the RUN session. The run has public id, agent, caller and state. It has NO public access to the completion token of the agents call that started it (AgentRun.context is internal). The token is in the Router record of the child session: RouterSessionDirectory.recordedChildren(of: caller) gives parentToolCallId for the run id. The announcer reads it once for each run. A run with no caller (a host run) has no tool call, so it gets no link.
+    2. TO VERIFY answer: when the observer sees the first event of a run, the join table is NOT guaranteed to hold the wire id. The root translator and the run are two tasks. Router gives the open record of the agents call to the translator before the body starts, but nothing orders the translator against the first event of the child. Order chosen: the queue step of the announcer waits for the entry (RunCallJoinTable.awaitToolCallId). The wait is event driven: it ends when the translator writes the entry, when the projection stops, or when the task is cancelled. It uses no time. The observer never waits; only the ordered queue step waits.
+    3. The agent has the retained history merge engine of the wire package. It folds subagent_update by session id, so the history of the parent already holds the current state of each child. The announcement goes through the history sink of the parent, so a resume replays it.
+    4. The ACP id of the parent is the caller ULID, or the root session for a host run. The place of the child (cwd, additional roots) is borrowed from the parent entry, as SessionBuild borrows it.
+    5. Known limits of this task, by design: no live Router session is attached, so a child run has no table entry in production yet. A grandchild whose parent run has no entry is not announced (blocked, and sent at a later observation after the entry exists). The final state of a run has no event after it, so the patch with the final state is sent at the next observation. The projection task owns the final state_update and the final tool_call_update order.
